quizzes.question: A marked table slides in and comes to rest 2 seconds before its scene ends. What does the frame check do?

options.label: It passes: at rest by the end
options.why: At rest by the end is the rule for a question's cards; a marked thing must be still for the whole last 3 seconds.

options.label: The frame fails the check
options.why: Right: the table still moves inside the scene's last 3 seconds, so the frame check fails the frame.

options.label: A note, not a finding
options.why: A note is for a mark whose size or place the frame's CSS does not say; a mark that moves late is a finding.

quizzes.explain: A marked thing must be at rest for its scene's whole last 3 seconds, so the button sits still over it; this table still moves in the first of them.
quizzes.walkMeThrough: The rule gives a marked thing its scene's last three seconds at rest, so the button over it never chases it. This table stops two seconds before the end, so it is still sliding for the first of those three seconds. The frame check fails the frame and says to bring it to rest three seconds before the end.

quizzes.question: A stop scene's choice cards are up, and the diff they are about is marked behind them. You click the diff. What happens?

options.label: Its page opens over the frame
options.why: The page opens from the thing only while no question's box is up; here the choice cards are up.

options.label: Nothing happens
options.why: Right: the choice cards are a question's box, so the diff's button hides and the click does nothing.

options.label: The first choice is accepted
options.why: Only a click on a choice's own card, or its Accept, answers it; the diff is not a card.

quizzes.explain: While a question's box is up, the marked thing's button hides, so a click on it does nothing; the button comes back once the box closes.
quizzes.walkMeThrough: A stop scene asks you to accept or flag its choices, so its box of cards is up. While any question's box is up, the marked thing's button hides, so the click on the diff does nothing. Once you answer and the box closes, the button comes back and the diff opens its page.

quizzes.question: The video is paused at 1:05 when you click a marked table. Its page opens, and you press Esc. What happens?

options.label: The video plays on from 1:05
options.why: The video plays on after a close only when it was playing as the page opened; here it was already paused.

options.label: It stays paused; focus on the table
options.why: Right: it was paused, so it stays paused, and focus goes back to the table's button.

options.label: The page moves to the side panel
options.why: Esc closes the page; nothing moves it to the side panel, which is kept only for the Terms and the band's long words.

quizzes.explain: Closing a page goes back to how the video was: it plays on only if it was playing, and focus returns to the thing that opened the page.
quizzes.walkMeThrough: The video was already paused at one minute five when you clicked the table, so opening its page changed nothing about playing. Esc closes the page and puts things back as they were: still paused. Focus goes back to the table's button, so Enter would open the page again.

quizzes.question: On a phone, a scene's marked code line shows 160 pixels wide and 30 tall. How does its page open?

options.label: By the button over the line
options.why: The button goes over the thing where it is tall enough to tap; on a phone that is 44 pixels, and this line is 30.

options.label: By the corner chip
options.why: Right: at 30 pixels tall on a phone it is under 44, so the corner chip opens the page instead.

options.label: It cannot open on a phone
options.why: Every page can be opened on a phone: where the thing is too small, the chip stays, and O opens it too.

quizzes.explain: On a phone, a marked thing under 44 pixels tall on screen is too small to tap, so the scene keeps the corner chip for its page.
quizzes.walkMeThrough: On a phone the player measures the marked thing as it shows on screen. This line is a hundred and sixty pixels wide but only thirty tall, under the forty-four a finger needs. So the scene keeps its corner chip, and the chip opens the page over the whole window.

calls.chose: `frame-lint` measures a marked thing from the frame's CSS (px `left`/`top`/`width`/`height`, insets, its parents'), padding counted unless `border-box`; a mark whose size or place the CSS does not say is a note, not a finding
calls.insteadOf: measuring each frame in a browser, or failing an unmeasured mark
calls.why: frame-lint is the cheap static check run as each frame lands, as its camera and card rules are; failing every unsized span would fail most pinned words, and the player guards at run time (no button on a thing too small to tap on a phone)

calls.chose: Two things marked with one name in a frame fail `frame-lint`
calls.insteadOf: a note, or the player taking the first
calls.why: the plan says one marked thing per detail, and the button goes over one box; a second would silently never open

calls.chose: "Landed" is read from the frame as it plays: the thing and everything holding it shown, at full opacity (≥ 0.95); until then there is neither the button nor the chip
calls.insteadOf: the end of its reveal read from the scene's timeline, or the button from the scene's start
calls.why: the page shows what is on screen whatever the timeline says (a fade, a camera, a later reveal), and a button over a thing still at 72 % would open a page about something not yet there
calls.check: detailMark in packages/player/reelplanning-player.js; packages/player/test/details.spec.mjs ("before the thing lands")

calls.chose: The button hides for as long as a question's box is up, an answered quick check counting down included, and comes back when it closes
calls.insteadOf: only while the question is unanswered
calls.why: while the box is up its cards carry the answer and their whys; one thing at a time on the frame
calls.check: syncDetailChip (!this._pendingDecision); spec "answered, the button comes back"

calls.chose: The button stays in the picture's layer, and the tab order reaches it by a hop: Tab from Play goes to it, Tab from it to what follows Play, Shift+Tab back (`tabHop`)
calls.insteadOf: moving the button after the controls in the page and placing it by script
calls.why: in the picture's layer it moves with the zoomed picture as the cards' buttons do, with nothing to keep in step; the hop gives the order the plan asks for

calls.chose: Every way in opens the page over the frame, the chip's and the plan text's too, grown from what was clicked (the chip, the thing; a list's opens without growing); the Terms and the band's long words keep the side panel
calls.insteadOf: over the frame only from the thing, the side panel from the chip and the list
calls.why: one place for a page whichever way it was opened; D-195 supersedes D-021's side panel, and the Terms and the band's words are not details
calls.check: openDetail, homeDetailPanel; spec "D-195: the page takes the video's box"

calls.chose: The ink ring is on the thing's button while its page is open, under the page (which covers the frame, D-195): it shows as the page grows and shrinks, and focus is on it once closed
calls.insteadOf: keeping the ring a few seconds after the page closes
calls.why: the plan's ring was written for a page beside the frame; with the page over it, the grow, the shrink and the focus back on the thing say what the page was about
calls.check: .dhit[data-open]; spec "while it is open, the thing keeps an ink ring"

calls.chose: O is logged by the way the scene offers: `from: "frame"` where its thing is marked, `"chip"` where the chip shows; a comment's link to its page in the record counts as `"list"`
calls.insteadOf: a fourth value for the key
calls.why: the record says which way in reviewers use, and O is the key for whichever the scene shows; the plan names three values
calls.check: openDetailFrom, endDetail; spec "logged from: frame" and "each says where it was opened from"

calls.chose: Each own-words field grows with its words to a cap and then scrolls inside the same box: 3 lines for the two note fields under an answer (the note on an answer, "Expected something else?"), 4 for the others (your own answer, a call's own words, the comment line, the record's editor); a note field is as wide as its placeholder, never its words
calls.insteadOf: one cap for every field, or growing with no cap
calls.why: the two note fields sit under an answer's cards, where more lines would push the cards and the controls; the owner asked to "keep same text box just be able to scroll it"
calls.check: fitField in packages/player/reelplanning-player.js; packages/player/test/own-answer.spec.mjs (stays within its cap, scrolls inside)

calls.chose: Enter still saves (or keeps a note) and Shift+Enter starts a new line; what is saved keeps its line breaks, runs of spaces folded to one and three or more breaks to two (`keepLines`), and the record's quick-check note no longer folds them away
calls.insteadOf: Enter for a new line with a button to save, or every break folded to a space as before
calls.why: Enter already saved every field, so a reviewer's habit stays; words in paragraphs say more, and a runaway paste stays readable
calls.check: keepLines and the fields' keydown in packages/player/reelplanning-player.js; packages/player/test/own-answer.spec.mjs ("saved whole with its line break")

plan.title: Details in the frame: click the thing a detail explains
plan.problem:
The owner, in the better-visuals walkthrough review:

> "we might want to work the detail pages more into the video so we dont just click a bar on the side, we
> instead click within the video kind of like we do for answering a question"

A detail is a page a scene opens for what the video cannot hold: the whole file, a table to sort, a
prototype to try (D-024: it starts from a template). Today you open it from outside the picture:

- **The Open chip.** While a scene has a detail, one chip sits in the stage's top-right corner: "Open · The
  data block and the slots · O". In the deep-dives walkthrough, scene 12 shows the real code, eight lines of
  `templates/details/table.html`; the detail is that file, whole, with the lines that carry the choice
  marked. The code is in the middle of the frame, and the way into it is a chip in the corner.
- **The plan text.** Each step's section ends with an "Open:" row naming its details.
- **The side panel** (D-021). Either one opens the page beside the paused video, 560 px wide on a
  1440 px window: the frame shrinks to the left, and the code gets less than half the width.

Answering already works the other way. Since the answer-in-the-frame plan, a question is answered on the
frame: each card carries `data-option`, the player lays a clear button over it, your pointer or focus rings
it in coral, "More" opens beside the card and never over the chips, and the lowest eighth of the frame is
kept for the answer bar. You click the thing you mean. A detail should open the same way: you click the code,
the table or the pinned word it explains.

steps.title: The frame marks the thing a detail explains, and the checks hold it
steps.text:
*Independent.*

A scene with `- detail: <name>` in the storyboard marks, in its frame, the one thing the page explains, with
`data-detail="<name>"` on that element:

- **a real thing** (a `data-artifact` region): the code block, the table, the terminal run. In deep-dives
  scene 12 that is the eight-line block of `table.html`.
- **a part of it**: one code line, one table row, one file on a map.
- **a pinned word** (its `data-gloss` label with the token under it): in the better-visuals plan video, the
  label "said too early: a warning" on `early.push` could open the rule's whole table.

One marked thing per detail, the smallest that is still what the page is about. The storyboard's
`- detail:` tag stays the source of which details a scene has (`- detail_title:`, `- detail_why:`); the frame
only says where. The skill's tag table, the style guide's §10 and the frame template say so, with the three
examples above.

The checks, so the player can trust the marked thing:

- **`frame-lint`** fails a marked thing that reaches the lowest eighth (y ≥ 945, where the answer bar goes), a marked thing
  under 120 × 44 px at 1920 × 1080 (a tap target), and one that is still moving in its scene's last 3 s:
  it, or a camera it sits in, has to be at rest, at scale 1, by then, as a question's cards are. It notes a
  marked thing that overlaps a `data-option` card.
- **`check-details`** (the details check, run by `finish-project`) fails a scene whose frame marks a name the
  storyboard does not give it. A storyboard `- detail:` with no marked thing in its frame is a △ warning, and a
  failure on a storyboard that carries `details_check: strict` (every new storyboard does, as it carries
  `terms_check: strict`). Older storyboards pass as they are.

steps.title: The player makes the marked thing a button
steps.text:
*Needs step 1's marked thing.*

The player finds the marked thing in the scene's own composition, the way it finds the cards (by `data-detail`,
inside the frame's `data-composition-id`), and lays a clear button over its box in the same layer as the
cards' buttons: it moves with the picture when you zoom past Fit (D-182), and a mark tool that is on takes the
frame, as for the cards.

- **What it draws** (question 1). The ring is the cards' ring: coral under your pointer or focus (D-179: the
  thing under your pointer is yours). The tab reads "Open · <the detail's title>"; hovering it for a moment
  shows the `detail_why` line beside it, placed as a card's "More" is, never over a control.
- **When it is there.** From the moment the marked thing lands (its reveal ends) to the end of the scene, and again
  whenever the video is paused on that scene. While a question or a choice is asked, the frame belongs to the
  cards: the detail's button hides and comes back when the question is answered.
- **While a question is up, a click on the thing does nothing.** Take a quick check on scene 12, whose block
  is marked: while the check is asked, the block has no button, no tab and no ring, so clicking the block
  opens nothing and answers nothing (only the cards answer). Answer the check first; the button comes back
  and the same click then opens the page. O, meanwhile, still means your own words (D-046), not the detail.
- **Keyboard.** The button is in the tab order after the play controls; Enter or O opens it, as O opens the
  chip today. Focus draws the same ring as a pointer.
- **Never over what you answer with.** Its tab sits on the thing's top edge, inside the frame and above the
  lowest eighth; where that would cover a card's button or a chip, it goes inside the thing's top-left
  corner instead.

steps.title: A click pauses the video and opens the page
steps.text:
*Needs step 2.*

A click on the thing, Enter on it, or O pauses the video and opens the detail. Where the page opens is
question 2 (the side panel today, D-021). Whichever way:

- **The thing stays marked.** While the page is open, the thing you clicked keeps an ink ring, so the frame
  says what the page is about when you come back to it.
- **Closing goes back.** ×, Esc or O closes the page; the video goes on from where it paused if it was
  playing, and focus returns to the thing's button.
- **The page keeps what it has.** Comments inside a page (anchored to a line or a row) and, in a walkthrough,
  a choice's Accept and Flag in the page's footer, work as today.
- **The record says where you opened it.** Each detail opened is logged with `from: "frame"`, `"chip"` or
  `"list"`, beside its time open (D-005: opening a page is not a rewind), so a later plan can see which way
  reviewers use.
- **The narration names the thing.** The style guide's `detail_why` rule gains one line: the sentence says
  what to click, "click the block to read the whole file".

steps.title: The corner chip and the plan text's list; older videos and phones
steps.text:
*Needs step 2.*

What becomes of the corner chip is question 3. The plan text's "Open:" row under each step stays in every
case: it is how you reach a detail from the keyboard without playing to its scene, and how you find one again
later.

- **Older videos keep working.** A detail whose frame marks nothing keeps today's corner chip, unchanged,
  until its video is rebuilt with its thing marked. Nothing in an older plan map or review changes.
- **Phones.** On a narrow stage (the player's `data-size="narrow"`), a thing whose box is under 44 px tall on
  screen is not a button (it would be too small to tap); that scene shows the chip instead (unless question 3 takes C: then the
  plan text's list), and the page covers the video as it does today.

glossary.meaning: Turns a plan into a video, via HyperFrames (plan.md in, a HyperFrames project out)
glossary.said: Turns a plan into a video, via HyperFrames.

glossary.meaning: Voices the script, only the lines that changed since the last build; reelplanning build runs it, then finish-project and verify
glossary.said: Voices the script, only the lines that changed since the last build; `reelplanning build` runs it, then finish-project and verify.

glossary.meaning: The assembly tail: captions → index → plan-map → the terms index (which video explains each word) → plan-diff → the details check
glossary.said: The assembly tail: captions → index → plan-map → the terms index (which video explains each word) → plan-diff → the details check.

glossary.meaning: Content-hash diff vs. the last committed build
glossary.said: Content-hash diff vs. the last committed build.

glossary.meaning: Which scenes of the system video a change to the system's description (spec.md), its parts (system.json) or this glossary reaches, so only those are rebuilt (reelplanning spec-diff); it also names a row no scene explains yet
glossary.said: Which scenes of the system video a change to the system's description, its parts or this glossary reaches, so only those are rebuilt; it also names a row no scene explains yet.

glossary.meaning: <reelplanning-player>: where you watch, answer on the frame, mark, and press Finish
glossary.said: Where you watch, answer on the frame, mark, and press Finish.

glossary.meaning: reelplanning review: serves the review page, takes the review when you press Send, keeps it in the inbox and hands it on once; sends the notifications
glossary.said: Serves the review page, takes the review when you press Send, keeps it in the inbox and hands it on once; sends the notifications.

glossary.meaning: The agent's own command (from config.json), started by the review server when no session is waiting; auto mode, inside the sandbox, or without it (and the reviewer told) where this machine can't run it
glossary.said: The agent's own command, started by the review server when no session is waiting; auto mode, inside the sandbox, or without it (and the reviewer told) where this machine can't run it.

glossary.meaning: The command that keeps the project record (scripts/reel.mjs, in .reelplanning/): reel record logs a review's answers and files the review; reel status ends with memory
glossary.said: The command that keeps the project record: `reel record` logs a review's answers and files the review; `reel status` ends with memory.

glossary.meaning: Acts on a plan review: approved, folds the comments into the plan (plan.md); changes requested, rewrites the steps a comment touched
glossary.said: Acts on a plan review: approved, folds the comments into the plan; changes requested, rewrites the steps a comment touched.

glossary.meaning: Builds what the plan says (plan.md) and logs each call the plan did not cover, with tags (in walkthrough.md); its diff is then checked by a second, fresh agent (the code check)
glossary.said: Builds what the plan says and logs each call the plan did not cover, with tags; its diff is then checked by a second, fresh agent (the code check).

glossary.meaning: Acts on a walkthrough review: changes the code for each flagged call; on changes requested, rebuilds only those beats
glossary.said: Acts on a walkthrough review: changes the code for each flagged call; on changes requested, rebuilds only those beats.

glossary.meaning: One video explaining the whole repo (from spec.md); rebuilt where the spec changes
glossary.said: One video explaining the whole repo; rebuilt where the spec changes.

glossary.meaning: One pass by a reviewer, filed once and never overwritten (reviews/<kind>-<time>.json, with a .md of what to act on). The player's download is annotations.json until it is filed
glossary.said: One pass by a reviewer, filed once and never overwritten. The player's download is `annotations.json` until it is filed.
files: `reviews/<kind>-<time>.json`, with a `.md` of what to act on

glossary.meaning: The verdict at Finish. Approve (on a walkthrough, the build is accepted): the comments are acted on, no new video. Request changes: they are acted on, the touched beats rebuilt, and the video shown again
glossary.said: The verdict at Finish. Approve (on a walkthrough, the build is accepted): the comments are acted on, no new video. Request changes: they are acted on, the touched beats rebuilt, and the video shown again.

glossary.meaning: .reelplanning/inbox/: reviews the review server has taken, each handed on once; not committed
glossary.said: Reviews the review server has taken, each handed on once; not committed.

glossary.meaning: The fence a headless run starts in: commands write only inside the repo, a hook keeps the file tools there too; checked before each run, and turned off, with the reviewer told, where it can't run (the hook stays)
glossary.said: The fence a headless run starts in: commands write only inside the repo, a hook keeps the file tools there too; checked before each run, and turned off, with the reviewer told, where it can't run (the hook stays).

glossary.meaning: A desktop notice from the review server: a video is ready, with what it will ask, or a headless run has ended
glossary.said: A desktop notice from the review server: a video is ready, with what it will ask, or a headless run has ended.

glossary.meaning: A choice the agent made on its own while building, one the plan did not cover (one row in walkthrough.md). Labelled *visible*, *hard-to-undo* or *close* when you might want to overturn it
glossary.said: A choice the agent made on its own while building, one the plan did not cover. Labelled *visible*, *hard-to-undo* or *close* when you might want to overturn it.

glossary.meaning: Which choices stop the walkthrough video: an off-plan change always, an unlabelled choice never, a labelled one until you have accepted that label ten times in a row, or again after a recent late fix with that label
glossary.said: Which choices stop the walkthrough video: an off-plan change always, an unlabelled choice never, a labelled one until you have accepted that label ten times in a row, or again after a recent late fix with that label.

glossary.meaning: What reviews show, worked out each time from the decision log and the filed reviews (reviews/), never kept by hand: the lines reel status ends with, the evidence behind each in reel memory <id>; the reviewer's own, across repos, from ~/.reelplanning/you.jsonl (--you)
glossary.said: What reviews show, worked out each time from the decision log and the filed reviews, never kept by hand: the lines `reel status` ends with, the evidence behind each in `reel memory <id>`; the reviewer's own, across repos, from `~/.reelplanning/you.jsonl`.

glossary.meaning: A late fix: something a review let through that a later plan, fix or review had to change. A recent one makes choices with its label stop the video again, however many were accepted in a row
glossary.said: A late fix: something a review let through that a later plan, fix or review had to change. A recent one makes choices with its label stop the video again, however many were accepted in a row.

glossary.meaning: A label the agent puts on a choice it made alone, saying why you might want to look at it. Four kinds: *visible* (you'll notice it when you use the thing), *hard-to-undo* (changing it later costs real work), *close* (a toss-up: the other way was nearly as good), *deviation* (an off-plan change). A labelled choice stops the walkthrough video; an unlabelled one does not
glossary.said: A label the agent puts on a choice it made alone, saying why you might want to look at it. Four kinds: *visible* (you'll notice it when you use the thing), *hard-to-undo* (changing it later costs real work), *close* (a toss-up: the other way was nearly as good), *deviation* (an off-plan change). A labelled choice stops the walkthrough video; an unlabelled one does not.

glossary.meaning: How many times in a row you accepted choices with the same label. At ten accepted in a row, choices with that label no longer stop the video; one flag starts the count again from zero
glossary.said: How many times in a row you accepted choices with the same label. At ten accepted in a row, choices with that label no longer stop the video; one flag starts the count again from zero.

glossary.meaning: An off-plan change: a choice where the agent did something other than what the plan said. It always stops the walkthrough video
glossary.said: An off-plan change: a choice where the agent did something other than what the plan said. It always stops the walkthrough video.

glossary.meaning: One scene of a video: a picture and a sentence or two of its voice. A video is a row of scenes; a question or a choice pauses at the end of its scene
glossary.said: One scene of a video: a picture and a sentence or two of its voice. A video is a row of scenes; a question or a choice pauses at the end of its scene.

glossary.meaning: A stretch of one video under one title; the player shows "Chapter 2 of 4" as it begins, and N / P jump between them. Not a plan's step, and not a part of the system
glossary.said: A stretch of one video under one title; the player shows "Chapter 2 of 4" as it begins, and N / P jump between them. Not a plan's step, and not a part of the system.

glossary.meaning: One part of the system, drawn as a box: the review player, the review server and the rest of this table's ids. system.json calls it a component; the system video says "part"
glossary.said: One part of the system, drawn as a box: the review player, the review server and the rest of this table's ids. `system.json` calls it a component; the system video says "part".

glossary.meaning: A plan of skill edits the memory's evidence supports, started when the status says one is due, and judged against a fixed benchmark (reel retro, reel status)
glossary.said: A plan of skill edits the memory's evidence supports, started when the status says one is due, and judged against a fixed benchmark.
